STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white square plate with a rim band and a flat centre, no curved inner wall. Flat square plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This plate looks medium-large, so about 24 cm.
b) Reference: the blueberries are about 1.5 cm across. The plate spans roughly 16 blueberry-widths... that is too small a reference to use reliably. Using the melon and watermelon cubes (about 2 cm each), the plate width spans roughly 11-12 cubes, giving about 22-24 cm.
Reconciled width: 23 cm, so area = 23 x 23 = 529 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Mashed potato / cottage-style white base: covers roughly 45% of the plate (about 240 cm²). It is a mound about 2 cm thick at its peak, averaging about 1 cm. Volume ≈ 240 cm³, mash density 1.0, so about 240 g.
- Green sauce (salsa verde / pesto-like): spread over the left portion of the mash, about 25% of the base area, thin layer about 0.3 cm. Volume ≈ 60 cm³ × 1.0 g/ml ≈ 60 g.
- Sweet potato cubes with sauce: cover roughly 15% of the plate (about 80 cm²), piled about 2 cubes high (~2 cm), averaging about 1.5 cm. Volume ≈ 120 cm³ × 0.6 density (chopped vegetable) ≈ 75 g.
- Melon (cantaloupe) cubes: about 10% of the plate, about 1.5 cm average thickness. Volume ≈ 80 cm³ × 0.6 ≈ 50 g.
- Watermelon cubes: about 12% of the plate, about 1.5 cm average. Volume ≈ 95 cm³ × 0.6 ≈ 55 g.
- Strawberry pieces: about 3% of the plate, roughly 1.5 cm thick. Volume ≈ 24 cm³ × 0.6 ≈ 15 g.
- Blueberries: about 6 visible, with a few hidden, so about 8 berries × 1 g (small berry ≈ 1 g each in this scale, counted at ~1.2 g) ≈ 10 g. Note the standard here is berries at about 1-1.5 g each.

Hidden food: no clear base beyond the mash, so no extra items added.

STEP 5 - Energy density (as served):
- Mashed potato, with green sauce mixed in: about 100 kcal/100 g (use mash ~90 kcal; sauce adds some).
- Green sauce: about 60 kcal/100 g.
- Sweet potato with sauce: about 100 kcal/100 g.
- Cantaloupe: about 34 kcal/100 g.
- Watermelon: about 30 kcal/100 g.
- Strawberry: about 32 kcal/100 g.
- Blueberries: about 57 kcal/100 g.

Estimated totals: about 615 g and roughly 1,000 kcal (mash ~240 g at 90 kcal ≈ 215 kcal; sauce 60 g ≈ 35 kcal; sweet potato 75 g ≈ 75 kcal; melon 50 g ≈ 17 kcal; watermelon 55 g ≈ 17 kcal; strawberry 15 g ≈ 5 kcal; blueberries 10 g ≈ 6 kcal). Sum is about 370 kcal, so the mash weight and sauce are the main uncertainties.
